bioprojects.title: Endotrypanum monterogeii strain:LV88 Genome sequencing and assembly
NHGRI Large Scale Sequencing Program for Organismal Sequencing

assembly_info.comments:
Background:
The Endotrypanum monterogeii LV88 strain was provided by Dr. Michael Chance, Liverpool, as described (A. H. Lopes, D.M. Iovannisci, M. Petrillo-Peixoto, D. McMahon-Pratt, & S.M. Beverley (1990), Molec. Biochem. Parasitol. 40: 151-162). It was isolated from a Choloepus hoffmani sloth in Costa Rica.
Genomic DNA was prepared by CsCl/Ethidium bromide density gradient centrifugation to minimize the amount of kinetoplast (mitochondrial) DNA, and was provided by Drs. Natalia Akopyants and Stephen Beverley, Washington University School of Medicine.
Total sequence coverage of 454 instrument reads was 50X (Fragments 20X, 3Kb PE 24X, 8Kb PE 6X) using a genome size estimate of 35Mb. The combined sequence reads were assembled using the Newbler software (Roche). This draft assembly was referred to as E_monterogeii_LV88_1.0.3. For the E_monterogeii_LV88_1.0 draft assembly 947 scaffold gaps were closed with Illumina read mapping and local assembly. Next error correction was done by aligning Illumina reads to correct insertion and deletion errors (4790). Finally, 33 contaminating contigs were removed and the scaffolds were arranged into chromosomes. This assembly version E_monterogeii_LV88_1.0.3 is made up of a total of 2558 scaffolds with an N50 scaffold length of over 697kb (N50 contig length was 33kb). The assembly spans 32Mb.

This work was supported by NIH grant AI29646 to SMB and by NIH-NHGRI grant 5U54HG00307907 to RKW, Director of The Genome Institute at Washington University.

For questions regarding this E_monterogeii_LV88_1.0.3 assembly please contact Dr. Wes Warren, Washington University School of Medicine (wwarren@genome.wustl.edu). Downloads of the sequence data are available via the TriTrypDB genome browser server. Funding for the sequence characterization of the Endotrypanum monterogeii LV88 genome was provided by the National Human Genome Research Institute (NHGRI), National Institutes of Health (NIH).
